Recent work supports separating evaluation artifacts from model failures. [RecSys 2025 leakage research](https://researchportal.helsinki.fi/en/publications/dont-get-ahead-of-yourself-a-critical-study-on-data-leakage-in-of/) reports sampled nDCG@10 drops of 21.7–73.4% after preventing temporal leakage; this concerns cross-user temporal leakage, distinct from exposing a prediction target inside bidirectional input. [Krichene and Rendle](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/) show sampled ranking metrics can reverse model comparisons even in expectation. Preserve the pinned host evaluator; use training-prefix holdouts to compare sampled and full-catalog rankings diagnostically, without replacing selection metrics.

Representation probes have relevant foundations. [ICML 2024](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v235/guo24e.html) identifies embedding collapse as concentration in a low-dimensional subspace; [spectral analysis, revised 2025](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.12008) connects dimensional collapse with amplified popularity bias. Useful measurements: centered embedding singular spectra/effective rank, pairwise cosine similarity, score dispersion, and ranking accuracy stratified by training-item frequency and history length. These are associations, not proof that collapse causes a particular BERT4Rec failure.

Proposed calibration protocol—not an established diagnostic recipe found in these sources: inject isolated faults into disposable evaluation copies, including visible targets, count-minus-one readout on left-padded inputs, disabled padding masks, and constant embeddings. Check whether probes distinguish faults and recover after restoration. Respect [BERT4Rec’s masked-target objective](https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.06690) and appended-mask inference. Report target rank plus margin (target score minus tenth-highest negative score) divided by candidate-score standard deviation; this is invariant to positive affine score transformations when variance is nonzero. Flag degenerate variance explicitly. Use findings to test masking, readout, regularization, or sampling changes within one trained BERT4Rec per category.
